text: A permanent magnet motor's rotor is magnetised whether or not the motor is powered. When fluid moving through the pump turns the shaft, the motor works as a generator and puts voltage on the power cable - up to about its rated voltage at its rated speed - with the drive switched off.

That can happen while the pump is run in or pulled, when fluid falls back through the pump after a shutdown, during an intervention or troubleshooting, and in a kick; after a fallback it can take a long time to settle.

Treat the cable, the penetrator and the junction box of a PMM well as live: ground and short the cable at the reel before work, wear rated insulating gloves when it must be handled ungrounded, follow the isolation procedure, and mark the wellhead as a PMM well. API RP 11S9 is the industry's recommended practice for PMM systems.
